heroHeadline: Day 377: Bilateral Freeze Hardens — International Bodies Warn of Rising Instability as Airspace Ban Continues to June 23
heroSubtitle: May 22, 2026: India-Pakistan ceasefire reaches Day 377 with the bilateral relationship at its deepest freeze since 1971. Pakistan FM Ishaq Dar renews calls for unconditional dialogue; India's precondition of 'credible and verifiable' counter-terrorism action remains unmet. Pakistan's airspace ban on Indian aircraft runs through June 23/24 (extended via NOTAM on May 19); India's reciprocal ban remains in force. Chatham House (April 2026) and The Diplomat (May 2026) both assess that the IWT dispute and absence of back-channel dialogue are the most dangerous unresolved dimensions of the post-Sindoor freeze. All bilateral mechanisms remain severed: $0 formal trade, no ambassadors, Indus Waters Treaty suspended (India rejected PCA's May 15 supplemental award), no confirmed progress toward any normalization. RSS General Secretary Hosabale's dialogue overture (May 12) continues to be met by BJP silence.
footerNote: Data sourced from Indian MEA/MOD, Pakistan ISPR/MFA, UN Security Council, SIPRI, Crisis Group, HRW, Stimson Center
